layman_headline: Solana is inching up but the broader market is pulling back — patience is the play.
layman_explanation: We already own Solana and it's up about 3% from where we bought it. The overall crypto market is dipping today with Bitcoin dropping nearly 3%, partly due to the Fed signaling they're still worried about inflation. Solana just passed a major vote to reduce its token supply faster, which is bullish long-term, but right now everything is in pullback mode. The swing candidates on offer today are either already extended (like AKE up 53% in a day), gold-backed stablecoins, or low-conviction plays with missing technical data.
layman_action: Hold your Solana position and let the trade play out toward the $115 target. Don't add new positions today — the setups aren't compelling enough given the market pullback. Keep your stop-loss at $92.
expert_reasoning: The current swing candidates are weak: AKE has surged 53% in 24h with no RSI/MACD data, making it a momentum-chasing trap. MON is down 44.5% from ATH with no clear reversal signals. XAUT/PAXG are gold-pegged tokens with minimal swing trade potential. PUMP is a meme-adjacent play with thin data. Our existing SOL position benefits from the just-passed disinflation vote (confirmed by CoinDesk and CryptoSlate — CryptoSlate is a reliable signal source per our credibility data). The Fed's hawkish tone from Warsh at Jackson Hole creates short-term headwinds, which explains today's broad pullback. With Fear & Greed at 68 (down from 73 yesterday), the market is cooling slightly but not panicking. Better to hold our winning position and wait for a higher-conviction entry on the next candidate.
risk_factors: Fed hawkish stance could push BTC below $75K and drag the entire market including SOL lower
SOL already up 8.8% on the week — a short-term pullback to retest $100 is plausible
Lack of RSI/MACD data on all swing candidates means we're flying partially blind on technicals
watch_list: BTC price action around the $75K-$78K support zone — a break lower would be bearish for all alts
SOL price behavior around $100 psychological support — if it holds, the uptrend is intact
Follow-up on Fed rhetoric post-Jackson Hole — any dovish pivot would fuel a broad rally
market_context: The crypto market is in a mild pullback with BTC down 2.9% after Fed Chair Warsh's hawkish comments at Jackson Hole. Fear & Greed has cooled from 73 to 68 but remains in Greed territory, suggesting no panic but caution is warranted.
context_banner: Market pulling back on Fed hawkishness — hold SOL with its bullish supply-reduction catalyst and wait for better entries elsewhere.

key_signals.description: Solana disinflation vote passed in dramatic finish, confirming a supply-reduction catalyst that supports medium-term price appreciation.
Kraken and Galaxy flipped late on the SOL vote — institutional interest in the supply change adds credibility to the bullish thesis (CryptoSlate has 67% win rate in our signal data).
Fear & Greed index dropped from 73 to 68 (Greed) — cooling but not alarming, suggesting a healthy consolidation rather than trend reversal.
Bitcoin dipped to $78.4K as Fed's Warsh downplayed softer inflation prints, creating macro headwinds for risk assets including crypto.
SOL's 24h volume of $5.4B is notably high relative to its market cap, indicating strong participation and conviction despite the pullback.
